notes: Only the mychart.org home page is saved. Several quotes come from help-menu text embedded in the saved .html (not shown in the .txt). The privacy policy is a link to epic.com and was not saved. No App Store listing is saved.

business_model.answer: Not stated directly. The page says MyChart is licensed from Epic Systems and that patients reach it through their own healthcare organization; no prices are shown. Epic as a whole reported about $5.7 billion revenue (FY2024, via a spokesperson).

evidence.quote: MyChart licensed from Epic Systems Corporation © 1999–2026
What is your healthcare organization's name?
annual revenue | $5.7 billion

who_uses_who_pays.answer: Patients use it for themselves and their family; accounts come through the patient's healthcare organization. Who pays is not stated.

evidence.quote: Manage care for you and your family
Find your MyChart

cost.answer: Not stated on its saved pages

how_they_differentiate.answer: They claim scale (over 190 million patients) and one login that pulls care together even across several healthcare organizations.

evidence.quote: Empowering over 190 million patients worldwide
Use one login for all your care
even if you've been seen at multiple healthcare organizations.

unique_value_proposition.answer: See and manage all your medical information and care in one place.

evidence.quote: MyChart lets you see your medications, test results, upcoming appointments, medical bills, price estimates, and more all in one place

retain_customers.answer: Not stated on its saved pages. The page lists everyday uses (results, scheduling, virtual visits) but no terms, tiers or retention features.

customer_experience.answer: Help is split: questions about care or your record go to your healthcare provider's office; technical questions go to Epic by email; there are help pages, scam warnings and a community training hub.

evidence.quote: Please reach out to your healthcare provider's office for help or to share feedback on your care.
For other questions, you can contact Epic at
Learn how to spot MyChart scams and protect your account from fraud.
Community training hub

relatives_joining.answer: Yes, through 'proxy access' to someone else's chart, which is handled by the patient's healthcare organization; the saved page links to it but does not give the steps or forms.

evidence.quote: Accessing someone else's chart (proxy access)
Get or give proxy access
Manage care for you and your family

privacy_data_consent.answer: Barely covered on the saved page: two-factor login, scam warnings, and account deletion or deactivation routed to the patient's healthcare organization. The privacy policy itself was not saved.

evidence.quote: Deleting/deactivating my account
Using two-factor authentication
Staying Safe from Scams and Fraud

emergencies.answer: MyChart is not for emergencies: the help screens tell people to call 911 (or 988 for mental health) and say the support form is for non-urgent technical help only. Support hours are not stated.

evidence.quote: For medical emergencies, dial 911 in the United States or your local emergency services number.
This form is for non-urgent technical help only.

setup.answer: The patient finds their healthcare organization's MyChart and creates an account there (or logs in with an Epic ID), on the web or the iPhone and Android apps.
